text:
Minnesota is rolling: 14-3-4, 32 points, a 10-game point streak (8-0-2) and seven straight road wins after Matt Boldy's hat trick in Toronto on Thursday. The Wild hold 56.3% of the expected goals, and our playoff race puts them at 99% to make it and 56% to win the division.

The engine is the top line. Joel Eriksson Ek, Kirill Kaprizov and Boldy have played 220 minutes together at 5-on-5, taken 63% of the expected goals, and outscored opponents 17-0. Kaprizov's NHL-leading 17th goal beat Montreal in overtime on Tuesday. Jesper Wallstedt is on a heater (.947 over his last five starts, 5-0-0, 7.8 goals saved above expected), and the team has allowed 14.4 fewer goals than its shots predicted. The record runs about five points ahead of the chances, mostly because of him.

The biggest story is Quinn Hughes. He's in the last year of his contract with no extension signed, and Sportsnet is running pieces asking whether he'll stay. On the ice he's everything they hoped: with Jonas Brodin he takes 56% of the expected goals, and with Jared Spurgeon 68%. And the Wild keep turning up in the Dylan Larkin trade talk, reportedly with the best offer on the table.

Maxim Shabanov (seven points in 10 games on 5.7 expected) and Michael McCarron are running hot in depth roles. Watch Wallstedt's save percentage settle, and watch Bill Guerin's phone, because John Hynes's team looks like a contender either way.
headline: The Wild are rolling, and Hughes is the question
